title: Monkey Republic
subtitle: A social simulation about trust, rules, and the world we build.

segments.caption: What happens when the same monkeys live under different rules?
segments.voiceover: What happens when the same monkeys live under different rules?

segments.caption: Monkey Republic is not just a game about bananas.
segments.voiceover: Monkey Republic is not just a game about bananas. It is a small society where students can test how trust, memory, rewards, and betrayal shape behavior.

segments.caption: Every monkey has two choices: share, or grab.
segments.voiceover: Every monkey has only two choices: share, or grab. But the numbers behind those choices change the world.

segments.caption: If sharing creates value, trust has room to grow.
segments.voiceover: In one world, sharing creates extra bananas. Trust has room to grow. In another world, sharing still helps a little, but betrayal hurts badly.

segments.caption: The first few rounds are slow, so students can see cause and effect.
segments.voiceover: The first few rounds are slow. Students can see who shared, who grabbed, how many bananas changed hands, and why one choice affects the next one.

segments.caption: Then the computer runs the society faster and faster.
segments.voiceover: Then the computer runs the society faster and faster. After a hundred rounds, patterns appear. Some monkeys become rich. Some lose trust. Some learn what the world rewards.

segments.caption: The takeaway is not a simple sentence. It is a question.
segments.voiceover: The takeaway is not a simple sentence. It is a question. Now that we can see how rules train strategy, how do we understand ourselves?

segments.caption: How do we think, create, search for significance, and contribute to real-world problems that matter?
segments.voiceover: In the age of AI, learning is not just about skills. It is about thinking with curiosity, creating through discovery, searching for significance, and contributing to real-world problems that matter.

segments.caption: Monkey Republic. A Lucas Academy social experiment.
